Remark
[Local boundary geometry] 1. ch14:14.1\group ch14-boundary-gradient Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0352 Let $\kappa (x_0)$ be the least principal curvature and $ u (x_0)$ the inner normal at $x_0\in \partial \Omega $. A boundary gradient estimate follows if, for each $x_0$, some neighborhood and nondecreasing $ ar\mu $ satisfy egin{equation} |a^{ij}D_{ij}\varphi +b| <\kappa (x_0)\mathcal T|p|+ ar\mu (|z|)\mathcal F ag {14.37} \end{equation} whenever $p-D\varphi $ is sufficiently large and its direction is sufficiently close to $\pm u (x_0)$. Then egin{equation} |Du|\leq C\qquad ext{on }\partial \Omega . ag {14.38} \end{equation} If $\kappa \geq \kappa _0$ globally, one may use the nonstrict inequality with $\kappa _0$. For example, for egin{equation} Qu=D_{11}u+(1+|D_2u|^N)D_{22}u=0,\qquad N\geq 0, ag {14.39} \end{equation} a boundary gradient estimate holds for arbitrary $C^2$ boundary data on a convex planar domain when the curvature is positive except possibly where the tangent is parallel to the $x_1$-axis.

The conclusions of this section depend only on the structural conditions in a neighborhood of $\partial \Omega $.
